title: Python Iterators
description: An iterator is an object that contains a countable number of values. An iterator is an object that can be iterated upon, meaning that you can traverse through all the values. In Python, an iterator is an object which implements the iterator protocol, which consists of the methods '__iter__()' and '__next__()'.
example:
// Common Iterator Usage
mytuple = ("apple", "banana", "cherry")
myit = iter(mytuple)

print(next(myit))
print(next(myit))

# Strings are also iterable objects
mystr = "banana"
myit = iter(mystr)
print(next(myit)) # 'b'

challenges.title: Next Value
challenges.exercise: Print 'next(myit)' to confirm you know how to get the next value from an iterator.
